How a guitar chord lesson works

  1. 1

    Fret the chord

    Each step shows one chord diagram with fingers, barres and the degree of every string: root, third, fifth and seventh.

  2. 2

    Listen and play along

    The app plays the chord string by string on a nylon-string guitar sound, then strums it, so you can check your fingering by ear.

  3. 3

    Play in time

    The final exercise chains every shape of the lesson to a metronome. Raise the BPM little by little — the app remembers your last tempo.

The fun way to learn guitar chords

Most guitarists know a handful of open chords and a couple of barre shapes, then get stuck. Chord charts with hundreds of diagrams are hard to memorise and even harder to use when a song changes key.

Guitar Workouts for Nerds turns that chart into a training plan. Instead of memorising shapes one by one, you learn the system behind them — five CAGED shapes and four seventh-chord inversions — and practise them in every key until they become automatic.

Guitar practice for busy people

Each exercise takes a few minutes: one chord, a handful of shapes, one run with the metronome. Do one key a day and you will cover the whole cycle of fourths in under two weeks.

Learn by playing, not by memorising charts

You never just look at a diagram. Every shape is fretted, heard and played in sequence, so your hands learn the fretboard and your ears learn the sound of each voicing.

Track your progress across all 12 keys

Every lesson has a variation for each of the 12 keys. A ring around the lesson fills in as you finish keys, and your last metronome tempo is saved next to each one.

Online guitar practice, nothing to install

Everything runs in the browser, on a computer, tablet or phone. The guitar sound is synthesised live.

Unlock the fretboard for any style

Pop, rock, MPB, bossa nova or jazz: chords in every key and position are what let you accompany a song anywhere on the neck, transpose on the fly and write smoother bass lines.

CAGED system exercises

The Basic Chords with CAGED module teaches the CAGED system: the five open-chord shapes — C, A, G, E and D — moved up the neck. You play major, minor, dominant seventh and half-diminished chords in all five shapes, from the lowest to the highest, in all 12 keys.

Chord inversion exercises for beginners and experts

The Seventh Chord Inversions module covers seventh-chord inversions: maj7, m7, 7 and m7(♭5) in root position and with the third, fifth and seventh in the bass, on the 4th, 5th and 6th strings — drop 2 voicings, plus drop 3 alternatives.

Triad inversion exercises

The Triad Inversions module covers major, minor and diminished triads in root position and with the third and fifth in the bass, on the 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th strings, in all 12 keys — a short way to play any chord anywhere on the neck.

Major scale exercises

The 7 Positions of the Ionian Mode module covers the major scale in seven positions, one shape per lesson, from the nut to the bridge, in all 12 keys.

Triad arpeggio exercises

The Triad Arpeggios module plays major, minor and diminished triads note by note — root, third and fifth — in three fingerings starting on the root, the third or the fifth, in all 12 keys.

Seventh chord arpeggio exercises

The Seventh Chord Arpeggios module plays maj7, m7, 7 and m7(♭5) chords note by note, starting on the root, the third, the fifth or the seventh, from the 6th, 5th and 4th strings, in all 12 keys.

Frequently asked questions

Is it free?

Yes. All lessons, the chord dictionary and the guides are free. You just create a free account to start practicing.

What is the CAGED system?

CAGED is a way of mapping the guitar neck with the five open-chord shapes C, A, G, E and D. Moving those shapes up the neck lets you play any chord in any key in five regions of the fretboard.

What are chord inversions?

A chord is inverted when a note other than the root is in the bass. A seventh chord has four notes, so it has root position and three inversions: third, fifth or seventh in the bass.

Do I need to read music?

No. Every chord is shown as a diagram with fingers and barres, and you can hear it before you play it.

Does it work on a phone?

Yes. The app works in any modern browser on phones, tablets and computers. Use headphones or a speaker to hear the low strings well.

Is it for acoustic or electric guitar?

Both. The shapes are the same on acoustic, classical and electric guitar in standard tuning (E A D G B E).
